---
title: Installation troubleshooting
description: "Diagnose optional plotting imports in container and Modal environments."
---

relflow's core modeling and training dependencies do not require Matplotlib.
CI installs the built wheel with only its required dependencies, then checks
import, one training step, checkpoint reload, and prediction. A second check
installs a complete plotting stack and exercises TorchMetrics plotting too.

## `No module named 'matplotlib.axes'`

This error can occur before model construction through Lightning and
TorchMetrics. In TorchMetrics 1.9.0,
[`utilities.plot`](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/torchmetrics/blob/v1.9.0/src/torchmetrics/utilities/plot.py)
imports Matplotlib when Lightning Utilities reports it as available. Lightning
Utilities 0.15.3
[`RequirementCache`](https://github.com/Lightning-AI/utilities/blob/v0.15.3/src/lightning_utilities/core/imports.py)
falls back to importing the top-level module when distribution metadata is
absent. An empty `matplotlib/` directory on Python's search path can import as
a namespace package and pass that check while providing no `matplotlib.axes`.

Run this inside the failing container or deployed function before importing
relflow:

```python
from importlib import metadata, util

for package in ("lightning", "torchmetrics", "lightning-utilities", "matplotlib"):
    try:
        print(package, metadata.version(package))
    except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
        print(package, "no distribution metadata")

spec = util.find_spec("matplotlib")
print("matplotlib origin:", None if spec is None else spec.origin)
print("matplotlib paths:", None if spec is None else spec.submodule_search_locations)
```

No spec and no distribution metadata describe an absent plotting dependency.
A spec with `origin=None` and search locations describes a namespace package;
inspect those paths for incomplete copied packages or source mounts. A normal
installation has distribution metadata and an `__init__.py` origin. Check the
deployed function as well as the image build, since their import paths may differ.

Remove unintended package directories from the image or mounted source. If the
workload uses plotting, install the complete distribution in the image rather
than copying selected Python files. For example, the Modal benchmark recorded
in [issue 67](https://github.com/relflow/relflow/issues/67) recovered with:

```python
image = image.uv_pip_install("matplotlib==3.10.7")
```

Set `MPLBACKEND=Agg` for noninteractive plotting. Verify `import relflow` and a
small training/prediction round trip in the deployed function after rebuilding.
A successful build-time import alone does not verify the deployed runtime.

The namespace-package reproduction matches the recorded exception and missing
distribution metadata locally and in the original Modal base image
(`im-euLinO1NW1JO5bbYRfpBAE`). A CPU sandbox using its installed relflow 0.4.0,
Lightning 2.6.6, TorchMetrics 1.9.0, and Lightning Utilities 0.15.3 imported
successfully without Matplotlib, failed with `matplotlib.axes` after adding an
empty namespace, and imported successfully after removing it. This tests the
base image; the source of the incomplete package in the original deployed 0.4.2
function remains unconfirmed. relflow does not replace upstream plotting
modules, patch dependency detection, or suppress unrelated import failures.

From a source checkout, the wheel smoke checks can be run in a separate virtual
environment containing the wheel and its required dependencies:

```bash
python scripts/imports.py --plotting absent
python scripts/imports.py --plotting namespace
# Install matplotlib==3.10.7 in this environment, then:
python scripts/imports.py --plotting installed
```

The namespace check creates an empty temporary package and verifies the specific
upstream failure in its own process. It leaves the installation untouched; the
other checks require successful modeling with absent or complete plotting support.
